newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's IG Metall ready to strike over sick pay.
newsitem.headline: Germany's IG Metall ready to strike over sick pay.

text.p: Germany's powerful IG Metall trade union is prepared to strike to keep sick pay benefits in forthcoming wage negotiations with employers, its leader Klaus Zwickel said late on Monday.

Sick pay, which is currently paid at the rate of full salary for six weeks, is expected to be cut to some 80 percent of pay as part of the German government's austerity package due to be voted on in parliament this Friday.
Zwickel told journalists that if sick pay is cut as part of the government savings plan, it would seek to retain the full level of payments in agreements with employers.
If negotiations failed, strikes would be likely, he added.
Some 240,000 trade union workers marched through half a dozen German towns at the weekend in protest at the planned austerity package, which they see as a full-frontal attack on welfare benefits.
Union leaders preparing to enter the forthcoming round of wage talks with employers have promised a "hot autumn" of labour unrest if the new legislation does go through.
